summary:
Trends is the story across every rating right now — R1, R2, and R3 all show identical 14-day trends splits at 62% (99-61, n=160), each running a full 5.6-point premium over season baseline, and trends+sp is the best category combo on the board at 57.9% (349-254, n=603). That combo matters today because DET is a full consensus play against WSN with all four ratings pointing the same direction (R3 leads at +1.02, R4 at +0.91), giving you a game where the hottest category in the model stacks directly on top of the day's strongest signal. Meanwhile bullpen_fatigue is ice cold across the board — every rating is riding a 6-game losing streak on that category at 48% over the last 14 days, well below season norms, so if bullpen_fatigue is pushing back against DET or MIN anywhere in your inputs, discount it hard today.

The rest of the slate is thinner. MIN @ SFG is a full consensus the other way — every rating likes SFG, with R2 showing the biggest gap at -0.88 — but Minnesota's Zebby Matthews starting and TOR/BAL below is a legitimate split, R1/R2/R4 lean BAL while R3 barely nudges TOR (-0.04), so treat that one as a pass or a small-side lean only. R4 deserves a mention independent of today's board: it's on a 4-game bullpen winning streak (59% last 14, n=160) and posted the best strong-play stretch of any rating over the last 14 days at 70% (45-19, +40.0u) and 65% over 30 days (105-57, +57.0u) — best win rate of the four ratings in every recent window despite the smallest season sample. If R4 is grouped with the trends+sp combo on DET tonight, that's about as strong a confluence as the model offers right now. Away from that, lean into BOS, LAD, and TBR if any appear soon — all three are hitting 70%+ when picked with strong-play multipliers, while NYY remains a fade at just 49% (21-22) and strong plays underwater at -5.0u.
